dlcservice: change to a normal (long-lived) system daemon See BUG field for rationale behind the decision. Here is a summary of what this CL does: 1. Remove dbus activation file. 2. Simplify init conf file. 3. Remove RAII-style shutdown scheduler. 4. Update unittest. 5. Set respawn/respawn limit in init conf file. Also I removed redundant dbus constants defs in system_api. Rationale about respawn limit: dlcservice takes a bit more than 1 sec (1 test-dlc installed) to boot: localhost ~ # time minijail0 -u dlcservice -g dlcservice -G -n /usr/sbin/dlcservice --load_installed=true real 0m1.147s user 0m0.016s sys 0m0.023s localhost ~ # time minijail0 -u dlcservice -g dlcservice -G -n /usr/sbin/dlcservice --load_installed=false real 0m1.088s user 0m0.017s sys 0m0.014s respawn limit 3 10 is a popular setting in src/platform and it works fine for dlcservice - respawn takes less than 2 seconds and if respawning more than 3 times in 10 seconds probably means it is less likely to recover. When more/bigger DLCs are added later, this limit may have to be revisited but it's hard to predict at this moment. BUG=chromium:905071 TEST=unittest, platform.DLCService TEST=below ~#for i in {1..20}; do echo "Loop $i"; killall dlcservice; sleep 1; done Loop 1 Loop 2 Loop 3 Loop 4 Loop 5 dlcservice: no process found Loop 6 dlcservice: no process found Loop 7 dlcservice: no process found Cq-Depend: chromium:1602938,chromium:1602563 Change-Id: I2d860827c0da5631008e15d296ce0049946005cf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1602894 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

sealed_storage: create a wrapper for Unseal To allow using the sealed_storage package in the components that can link ChromeOS libraries (libchrome, libbrillo), but don't have an easy way to include their header files, create a wrapper around SealedStorage class interface that doesn't require including those headers to use and can be used with components compiled by a different compiler: extern "C" and no non-trivial types in the API. gooftool: wipe: don't delete .developer_mode if GBB flags are not cleared In early build, we might decide to keep GBB flags so we can stay in developer mode. In this case, clobber-state will still generate '.developer_mode' tag in stateful partition, and wipe will still delete it. So on next boot (in release image), Chrome OS can't find the tag, and will start power washing immediately, which is time consuming. To prevent this, add code to detect if GBB flags are cleared, if not and dev switch is forced on, we won't delete the tag. arc-build: Support building for ARCVM. This adds an arc-build-constants eclass and an arc-build-constants-configure method that will setup ARC_PREFIX, ARC_VENDOR_DIR, and ARC_ETC_DIR for use with ARCVM. Bluetooth: add quick test infrastructure The Bluetooth quick test infrastructure provided a way to quickly run aset of tests.As for today, auto-test ramp up time per test is about 90-120 seconds, where a typical Bluetooth test may take about 30-60 seconds to run. The quick test infrastructure, implemented inthe BluetoothAdapterQuickTests class, saves this huge overhead by running only the minimal reset and cleanup operations between each set of tests (takes few seconds). The class BluetoothAdapterQuickTests provides wrapper function to start and end a test, a batch or a package. A batch is defined as a set of tests, preferably with a common subject, e.g 'LE Sanity' batch. A package is a set of batches. The class takes care of tests, batches, and packages test results and prints out summaries of results. The class also provides peer reset and cleanups between tests, batches, and packages. A batch can also be run as a separate auto-test. There is a place holder to add a way to also run a specific test of a batch autonomously. A batch can be implemented by inheriting from the BluetoothAdapterQuickTests class, and using its quick_test wrapper functions. A package can be implemented by inheriting from a set of batches. Adding a test to one of the batches is as easy as adding a method to the class of the batch. This CL implement two batches - 'LE Sanity' and 'Stand Alone Sanity', and one package - 'BT Quick Sanity' that run both these batches. FROMGIT: ACPI: PM: Set enable_for_wake for wakeup GPEs during suspend-to-idle I noticed that recently multiple systems (chromebooks) couldn't wake from S0ix using LID or Keyboard after updating to a newer kernel. I bisected and it turned up commit f941d3e41da7 ("ACPI: EC / PM: Disable non-wakeup GPEs for suspend-to-idle"). I checked that the issue got fixed if that commit was reverted. I debugged and found that although PNP0C0D:00 (representing the LID) is wake capable and should wakeup the system per the code in acpi_wakeup_gpe_init() and in drivers/acpi/button.c: localhost /sys # cat /proc/acpi/wakeup Device S-state Status Sysfs node LID0 S4 *enabled platform:PNP0C0D:00 CREC S5 *disabled platform:GOOG0004:00 *disabled platform:cros-ec-dev.1.auto *disabled platform:cros-ec-accel.0 *disabled platform:cros-ec-accel.1 *disabled platform:cros-ec-gyro.0 *disabled platform:cros-ec-ring.0 *disabled platform:cros-usbpd-charger.2.auto *disabled platform:cros-usbpd-logger.3.auto D015 S3 *enabled i2c:i2c-ELAN0000:00 PENH S3 *enabled platform:PRP0001:00 XHCI S3 *enabled pci:0000:00:14.0 GLAN S4 *disabled WIFI S3 *disabled pci:0000:00:14.3 localhost /sys # On debugging, I found that its corresponding GPE is not being enabled. The particular GPE's "gpe_register_info->enable_for_wake" does not have any bits set when acpi_enable_all_wakeup_gpes() comes around to use it. I looked at code and could not find any other code path that should set the bits in "enable_for_wake" bitmask for the wake enabled devices for s2idle. [I do see that it happens for S3 in acpi_sleep_prepare()]. Thus I used the same call to enable the GPEs for wake enabled devices, and verified that this fixes the regression I was seeing on multiple of my devices. [ rjw: The problem is that commit f941d3e41da7 ("ACPI: EC / PM: Disable non-wakeup GPEs for suspend-to-idle") forgot to add the acpi_enable_wakeup_devices() call for s2idle along with acpi_enable_all_wakeup_gpes(). ] Fixes: f941d3e41da7 ("ACPI: EC / PM: Disable non-wakeup GPEs for suspend-to-idle") Link: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=203579 Signed-off-by: Rajat Jain <rajatja@google.com> [ rjw: Subject & changelog ] Cc: 5.0+ <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.0+ Signed-off-by: Rafael J. CHROMIUM: devfreq: Fix rk3288_dmc / cpufreq interactions When I switched my device over to the "schedutil" governor and it was sitting on the sign in page (instead of the spinning login animation) I started seeing _tons_ of devfreq timeouts spamming my console. I did a tad bit of debugging and found that something about the way rk3288_dmcfreq was trying to lock the CPU Frequency just wasn't working. Specifically I printed the frequency of "pll_apll" when I was seeing a timeout and found that it was really low. Instead of debugging why the old way of doing things didn't work anymore, I decided to just switch rk3288_dmc to request a higher CPU Frequency by using the cpufreq notifiers. That's what everyone else does and is the supported way. It seems to work great. As a side effect of this it turns out that we can easily override the CPU Frequency that thermal throttling (and, actually, sysfs) imposed on the system. Thinking about this it actually seems like a beneficial thing to do. Sure we'll temporarily bump up to a really high CPU when we're hot, but we'll very quickly bump back down. ...and overall we may save power because we won't get so many failed transitions and we'll also spend less time with all CPUs spinning waiting for the transition to be done.
